uncertain.note: marker key a is not present in the body column: the italic 'a' printed at this height sits in the margin column, aligned with the note's other lines, so it is the note key and not a body marker
marker key b is not present in the body column: the italic 'b' beside body line 5 of the annotation is left-aligned with the note's following lines, so it is the note key and not a body marker

the glyph between 'Cluentio.' and '. de' is a short flagged stroke, not the tall looped italic l used in notes b and c; it could equally be the numeral '1'. Read as 'l.' on the sense of the citation (l. debitores, C. de pignor.)
a heavy ink mark sits over the final n of 'en'; probably show-through or a broken sort rather than a tilde, but 'eñ' cannot be ruled out
the mark after 'vrb' is two dots, the upper one thin and irregular; read as a colon, but it could be a period plus a speck
no period is visible after the 'c' here (contrast note g, where 'c.' is clearly pointed); no period is visible after 'eccleſiaſtic' on the preceding line either
the final letter is a tall C; could be a lowercase c set large, and the word order 'Tite iij. C.' is unusual for this book's citations
the word-break sign after 'Leuiti' is faint and partly lost in the paper; supplied as a hyphen because 'que' opens the next line
the two final I's of the numeral carry dots in the spaced-capital fount; transcribed as XVII
